description: Student believes that conditional statements, i.e., Python statements that evaluate to either True or False, must be explicitly compared to True or False to be used in conditionals.
Student believes that loop variables are destroyed and are inaccessible after the loop completes.
Student believes that the = operator is used for equality comparison in conditional statements.
Student believes that colons (:) are used for variable assignment.
Student believes that in the expression x == a or b, the comparison operator distributes to both operands of the or operator.
Student believes that for loop variables exist in a separate scope and won't affect variables with the same name in the enclosing scope.
Student believes that it is unnecessary for loop variables to be explicitly initialized before the loop.
Student believes that modifying a for loop variable inside the loop body does not affects the next iteration's value.
Student believes that conditional statements, i.e., Python statements that evaluate to either True or False, must always be wrapped in if/else statements to be returned as Boolean values.
Student believes that multiple mutually exclusive conditions in a control flow construct must each be written as separate if statements.
Student believes that values must be explicitly converted to their current type to ensure type safety.
Student believes that while loops execute their body only once if the condition is true.
Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.
Student believes that the and operator always evaluates both operands.
Student believes that the or operator always evaluates both operands.
Student believes that a variable assigned an arithmetic expression containing other variables automatically updates its value when those variables change.
Student believes that variable identifiers can only be one letter long.
Student believes that variable names containing vowels can only store string values, while consonant-only names can store any type.
Student believes that the arithmetic operation + has higher precedence than the arithmetic operation /.
Student believes that the arithmetic operation - has higher precedence than the arithmetic operation /.
Student believes that the arithmetic operation + has higher precedence than the arithmetic operation *.
Student believes that the first character of a string is at index 1.
